# Runtime and Economics Principles {.unnumbered}

Agentic workloads combine intermittent inference, tool latency, persistent state, branching execution, and recovery. Their runtime must schedule heterogeneous work while accounting for the outcome produced, not merely tokens served or devices occupied.

::: {#pri-durable-execution .callout-principle title="Durability follows the control state"}

**Invariant**: A recoverable trajectory must persist the decisions and effects needed to reconstruct its control state after interruption.

**Implication**: Checkpoint boundaries should follow semantic progress and external side effects rather than arbitrary token or wall-clock intervals alone.

:::

::: {#pri-reuse-correctness .callout-principle title="Reuse is conditional"}

**Invariant**: Cached computation or state may be reused only when its identity, dependencies, and authorization context remain valid.

**Implication**: Prefix, result, and memory caches need correctness and privacy keys as well as performance keys.

:::

::: {#pri-verified-economics .callout-principle title="Optimize verified outcomes"}

**Invariant**: Resource efficiency is meaningful only relative to an outcome that satisfies the task's verification criteria.

**Implication**: Cost per token or per step can improve while cost per acceptable result worsens through retries, rework, or undetected failure.

:::
